**Triage** — `domain:devx`, `documentation`, **`pm:blocked`**.

Blocked-by: #11407

Restart-when: #11407 closes (its PR **#11652** merges).
Unlock-action: re-grade to `pm:queue`; the fix must **flip** #11652's pinned skip list, not delete it.

## Ruling: route 1 only. ⛔ Route 2 is out of scope for this card.

Re-author the four fragments into shapes the existing discriminator already admits. Do **not** widen the selector.

The reason is the one #11407's dispatch already gave and this report already honours: a `{ name, type }` object literal at fragment top level is *probably* a field def, and "probably" is precisely what a layer discriminator must refuse. Widening it would buy four doc examples at the cost of the property that makes the gate trustworthy — that every admitted site's layer is *read off the structure*, never inferred. The gate's value is entirely in what it declines to judge.

Route 1 also produces something route 2 cannot: for `layout-dsl.mdx`, the layer currently lives **only in a prose comment** (`// e.g. on a FormSection / FormField`). Wrapping those in the real shape makes the layer explicit to human readers, not just to the parser. That is the better documentation independently of the gate, which is what makes this worth doing rather than a gate-appeasement edit.

## ⚠️ The thing that will bite whoever takes this

Re-authoring the four moves them from **skipped** to **admitted**: the gate's counts go from `13 admitted / 7 skipped` to `17 admitted / 3 skipped`. #11652 **pins those numbers in `--self-test`**, and pins that the skip list prints on green runs.

So this card **must flip existing pins**, exactly the way #11584's pin was flipped by #11542 rather than deleted. A fix that gets to green by deleting the assertions has removed the only thing standing between this gate and silent drift. Expect to touch the self-test, and say in the PR body which pinned numbers moved and why.

⭐ And when the four become admitted, they get **judged** for the first time. Verify all four actually pass the field-level rule before re-authoring — if one of them turns out to be a live defect, that is a separate and more interesting card, not something to fold in silently under a docs-shape change.

## The three that stay skipped are correct, and must stay skipped

`flows.mdx:320` (screen flattens its own field names, so the bare reference is right), `pages.mdx:165` (page component genuinely binds `current_user`), `views.mdx:415` (`fields:` **array**, the shape form views / flow screens / action params share). Judging any of these by the field-level rule produces a **false red on correct documentation** — worse than no gate. ⛔ Do not "fix" them into admission.

Two of the seven skips being exactly the false reds a key-keyed gate would have produced — in today's corpus, not hypothetically — is the strongest single piece of evidence that #11407 chose the right discriminator. That belongs in the record here, not just in the PR.

## The ruling stands, unchanged

**Route 1 only** — re-author the four fragments into shapes the discriminator already admits. ⛔ Do **not** widen the selector. Full reasoning in the triage comment above; the short version is that the gate's worth is entirely in what it declines to judge, and "probably a field def" is exactly what a layer discriminator must refuse.

## Re-stating the two traps, now that they are live rather than hypothetical

⚠️ **This card must FLIP pins, not delete them.** #11652 pins `13 admitted / 7 skipped` and pins that the skip list prints on green runs. Re-authoring the four moves those to `17 admitted / 3 skipped`. A fix that reaches green by deleting the assertions has removed the only thing standing between this gate and silent drift — the same shape #11584's pin was flipped by #11542 rather than dropped. Say in the PR body which pinned numbers moved and why.

⭐ **Judge the four before re-authoring them.** The moment they become admitted they get *evaluated* for the first time. If one turns out to be a live defect rather than merely an unreachable shape, that is a separate and more interesting card — surface it, do not fold it silently into a docs-shape change.

⛔ **The three genuinely-other-layer skips stay skipped**: `flows.mdx:320` (a screen flattens its own field names, so the bare reference is correct), `pages.mdx:165` (a page component really does bind `current_user`), `views.mdx:415` (`fields:` array). Judging any of them by the field-level rule produces a false red on correct documentation — worse than no gate.

## Closing — PR #11672 landed. Ruling **A** on the open question.

Verified by content on `origin/main`, landing commit located by `(#11672)` in its subject:

```
721ca92da  docs(formulas): pin the raw predicate example to the object-field layer (#11672)

content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx
  name: 'rating'        1 -> 0
  ObjectSchema.create   1 -> 2
  CTRL Field.text(      2 =  2      (steady, non-zero both sides)
  CTRL visibleWhen      4 -> 6
```

PR says `Part of`, so no keyword fired; closing by hand rather than spending a CI cycle on a one-word body edit. `pm:dispatched` stripped.

## ⭐ The corrected partition — recorded here, not only in a merged PR body

This is the reason the card closes rather than the reason it was opened, so it belongs on the card:

**The 4 re-authorable / 3 permanent split in this report was wrong. The measured split is 1 / 6.**

Only `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx:279` was an authoring-shape skip. The three `layout-dsl.mdx` sites are genuinely other-layer, and each states its layer in its own comment one line above the predicate. The decisive one:

```
layout-dsl.mdx:862   // On a PageComponent, an app/nav entry, or a per-option `visibleWhen`:
layout-dsl.mdx:863   visibleWhen: "'sales_manager' in current_user.positions"
pages.mdx:165        visibleWhen: "'sales_manager' in current_user.positions",
```

**Byte-identical predicates.** `:863` returns the same *"`current_user` is unbound here"* error that `pages.mdx:165` would — and `pages.mdx:165` is the skip #11407's ruling protects **by name** as a false red on correct documentation. So a site sitting in the "probably re-authorable" bucket was in fact a member of the protected class.

`:821` and `:824` are a matched pair whose whole purpose is contrasting PageComponent bindings against FormSection/FormField bindings. Authoring either half as a `Field.*` factory or a `fields:` map would assert the object-field layer — a *different* layer from the one the line exists to illustrate — and destroy the contrast that is the fence's entire content. The file documents the objectui layout DSL and contains no object-field example at all.

⭐ **So `14 admitted / 6 skipped` is the honest ceiling, not the 17/3 this card projected — and that is a stronger result for #11407's discriminator than the card claimed**: after this change, every site the gate declines to judge is one where judging it would be wrong.

## Two things this run got right that the brief did not ask for

**It judged the four before touching them.** That is the only reason the protected-class member was caught. Had it re-authored first and judged after, `:863` would have shipped as a false red against correct documentation.

**It kept a fixture that looked obsolete.** `'SKIPPED — a bare field-def fragment with no `fields:` map above it'` survives deliberately: this PR removed that shape from the corpus, which makes the synthetic fixture the **only remaining guard** that the discriminator still refuses it. Deleting it would have sounded reasonable and been wrong.

## My own error, since it is what this card cost

My binding ⛔ ruling demanded a target of `17 admitted / 3 skipped` **and** protected `pages.mdx:165` by name. Those two instructions contradict each other, because `:863` is that same predicate. I also asserted that #11652 pinned `13/7` in `--self-test` — **it does not**; `FIELD_RULE_SELF_TEST_CASES` holds synthetic per-shape fixtures, never a corpus total, and `--self-test` reports 48 cases unchanged on both sides. So one of my ⛔s was based on a pin that does not exist and pointed at a target unreachable without asserting a false layer.

The root cause is measured and filed: **#11673** — the skip list's reasons say why the *parser* stumbled, never what layer the *document* is about, so the list cannot be triaged from the list. Three independent passes (this report, my triage, my dispatch) landed on the same wrong partition. That card is graded `pm:queue` with the ruling that a skip may **show** context but must never **conclude** from it.

Closing `completed`.
